local_articles.title: Real Madrid make it three from three under Mourinho as Bellingham, Mbappe inspire 4-0 Malaga rout
local_articles.snippet: Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe both struck as Real Madrid's perfect start to La Liga under Jose Mourinho continued in a 4-0 cruise against Malaga on Sunday. Los Blancos scored three times in just over 10 minutes in the first half to open up a comfortable lead over the Andalusian visitors to the Santiago Bernabeu. {{^htLoading}} {{/htLoading}} Sandwiched between Bellingham and Mbappe's strikes was an own goal by Malaga goalkeeper Alfonso Herrero, while Arda Guler tapped in a fourth late on. "I've got the freedom to go higher or lower if we need, I'm enjoying myself a lot," Bellingham told Real Madrid TV of his attacking midfield role under Mourinho. The former Birmingham and Borussia Dortmund star was given a standing ovation from the fans when he was substituted in the second half. Simultaneously, MSF announced Friday it opened a new emergency treatment center in Beni, North Kivu (122 confirmed cases, 87 deaths, ~69% CFR), calling it one of the hardest-hit areas. Combined with ECDC's Aug 26 finding that North Kivu accounts for 78% of confirmed cases outside Ituri (735 cases, 501 deaths) amid M23 displacement and insecurity, North Kivu strengthens further as the prime candidate for WHO's mid-September surging-cases assessment (0.39 -> 0.47). Meanwhile, frontline Ervebo vaccinations launched Thursday in Kisangani (Tshopo) moving in a ring around Ituri. Haut-Uele remains a serious #2 surge risk (0.27 -> 0.23; ETC collapse and weak tracing), followed by epicenter Ituri (0.18 -> 0.16), Bas-Uele (0.08 -> 0.07), and Tshopo (0.06 -> 0.05), leaving 0.02 residual for other provinces.
